title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Staff
tiers.description: Directors, officers, employees, consultants and contractors of Pacific Niugini and its related entities.

tiers.name: Senior Management
tiers.description: The Board, the Chief Executive Officer or any other senior executives, and the Company Secretary. Required to obtain prior written approval before any trading.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Members of the Board (a subset of Senior Management); separately required to notify the Company Secretary of initial and ongoing holdings.

tiers.name: family member
tiers.description: Spouse or partner, parents or parents-in-law, children/stepchildren, and the spouses/partners of any of those people. Dealing by a family member is discouraged except outside a prohibited period; not a formal prohibition.

definitions.hedging_definition: dealing in financial products issued or granted over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities which have the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements

windows.start_anchor: one month before the announcement of Pacific Niugini's quarterly results (or, if shorter, from the end of the relevant quarter)
windows.end_anchor: announcement of Pacific Niugini's quarterly results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may notify Staff of any other period when trading is prohibited, imposed from time to time when the Company is considering matters subject to Listing Rule 3.1A, which may include periods preceding annual or half-year results containing unpublished price sensitive information. Confidentiality of such a notified period is not addressed.

rules.detail: Staff may deal in securities or derivatives outside a prohibited period provided they do not hold price sensitive information; the transaction must be reported to the Company Secretary once completed.
rules.evidence: A person ('the insider') who possesses inside information about a company must not apply for, acquire, or dispose of a company's securities or derivatives or procure someone else to do these things for them.

rules.detail: Senior Management require prior written approval before any trading, which is not limited to on-market share trades and would extend to entering an OTC derivative given securities are defined to include financial products created over Pacific Niugini securities.
rules.evidence: Senior Management are required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

rules.detail: The ban is limited to prohibited periods; it does not purport to ban hedging of unvested entitlements outside those periods, which would instead fall under the general dealing/derivatives rules (Senior Management approval; Staff must avoid price sensitive information).
rules.evidence: The dealing in financial products issued or granted over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities which have the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements is prohibited during a prohibited period.

rules.detail: Clause 3.4 addresses only unvested entitlements; hedging of vested, unrestricted holdings is not separately named and would be treated as an ordinary dealing in financial products (see the derivatives topic).

Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards are not named but are conditional contracts to sell securities, which the dealing definition expressly captures; permitted outside a prohibited period without prior clearance, subject to post-trade reporting.
rules.evidence: Legally there are many forms of dealing such as granting options over shares, entering conditional contracts to buy or sell securities and so on.

rules.detail: A monetisation transaction is 'trading' for the purposes of the prior written approval requirement.
rules.evidence: Senior Management are required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named separately; the dealing definition covers selling with no ownership qualification, so it is treated the same as any other dealing (prohibited-period and price-sensitive-information limits apply).
rules.evidence: For the purpose of this Policy, dealing includes buying, selling, subscribing for any Pacific Niugini securities, whether on your own account or on behalf of another person.

rules.detail: Caught by the prior written approval requirement covering 'any trading'.
rules.evidence: Senior Management are required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and is not a form of 'buying, selling or subscribing' captured by the dealing definition.
Not named, but securities are defined to include any financial product issued or created over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities, which covers a CFD.
rules.evidence: securities are any listed or unlisted class of share, right, option, warrant, convertible note, bond, debenture, or any financial products issued or created over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities.

rules.detail: Caught by the prior written approval requirement covering 'any trading'.
rules.evidence: Senior Management are required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

rules.detail: No provision addresses margin loans or a lender's forced sale of Pacific Niugini securities.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not named as a form of dealing; only 'granting options over shares' is given as an example of dealing.
No provision addresses secured financing of any kind in respect of Pacific Niugini securities.
No holding period, intention test or buy-sell window is stated beyond the prohibited periods themselves.

clearance.approver: Chairman, or in his absence, two directors
clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Once you have completed a transaction')
clearance.evidence: Senior Management are required to obtain prior written approval from the Chairman, or in his absence, the approval of two directors prior to any trading being undertaken.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Once you have completed a transaction')
clearance.evidence: You can deal in Pacific Niugini securities outside of the prohibited periods, unless you hold price sensitive information. Once you have completed a transaction you must report details of the transaction to the Company Secretary.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Directors of Pacific Niugini are required to notify the Company Secretary details of: ... all changes in Pacific Niugini securities they hold directly or indirectly within 2 days of the transaction occurring.

exceptions.evidence: transfers of securities where the beneficial ownership of the securities does not change, e.g. the transfer of securities already held into a superannuation fund where the Staff is a beneficiary
the exercise of an option or a right, or the conversion of a convertible security, where the final date to exercise the option or right, or convert the security, falls during a prohibited period
undertakings to accept, or acceptance of, takeover offers
trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the Company's security holders, such as a rights issue, security purchase plan, a dividend reinvestment plan or securities buy-back

Staff, who are not in the possession of price sensitive information, may be given prior written clearance by the Board to sell or otherwise dispose of Pacific Niugini during a prohibited period, where the Staff is in severe financial difficulties or other exceptional circumstances determined by the Board
such as required under a court order, in a bona fide family settlement, or some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so

exemption_authority: The Board may give prior written clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of securities during a prohibited period for Staff not in possession of price sensitive information who are in severe financial difficulties or other exceptional circumstances determined by the Board (court order, bona fide family settlement, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement).

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging ban limited to unvested entitlements and prohibited periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: The dealing in financial products issued or granted over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities which have the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements is prohibited during a prohibited period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only express hedging restriction targets unvested entitlements and only bites during a prohibited period; a collar over vested, unrestricted shares taken outside a prohibited period is not expressly banned by this clause.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no secured financing or encumbrance provisions
bespoke_clauses.clause: (the policy contains no reference to margin loans, secured financing, granting security, or a lender's forced sale)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: On the face of this policy a bank loan secured on the collared shares is not addressed and therefore not prohibited, though Senior Management would still need pre-approval to enter into the collar/loan transaction itself as 'trading', and a forced sale by the bank during a prohibited period would still be a dealing needing separate justification.

bespoke_clauses.clause: securities are any listed or unlisted class of share, right, option, warrant, convertible note, bond, debenture, or any financial products issued or created over or in respect of Pacific Niugini securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because this definition has no venue limitation, an OTC put and call are dealings requiring the same clearance and window compliance as an on-market trade.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealing in Pacific Niugini securities by a family member is to be discouraged, except outside a prohibited period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or loan routed through a spouse or family trust is not formally prohibited, only discouraged, and there is no enforceable associate-dealing regime to navigate around.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Once you have completed a transaction you must report details of the transaction to the Company Secretary. Directors ... all changes in Pacific Niugini securities they hold directly or indirectly within 2 days of the transaction occurring.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry into, and any variation or close-out of, the collar or loan must be reported to the Company Secretary (within 2 days for Directors), making the bank relationship visible to the Company even though it is not itself restricted.

summary: A funded collar appears possible under this policy, subject to timing and approval rather than an outright ban. Senior Management (the Board, CEO/senior executives and Company Secretary) must obtain prior written approval from the Chairman (or two directors) before entering the OTC put/call, which is caught as 'trading' given securities are defined broadly to include financial products created over Pacific Niugini securities with no venue limit; other Staff may deal without prior approval, subject only to reporting afterwards. The transaction must be entered outside the one-month pre-quarterly-results prohibited period (and any other Company-notified prohibited period) and while not in possession of price sensitive information; the only express hedging restriction (clause 3.4) is confined to unvested entitlements and to prohibited periods, so a collar over vested, unrestricted shares taken in an open window is not banned by that clause. The policy is silent on margin lending, encumbrance and secured financing entirely, so the loan leg secured on the collared shares is not addressed, though a forced sale by the bank lender during a prohibited period is not carved out as an exception and could require separate hardship-style Board clearance. Directors must notify the Company Secretary of the resulting change in their holdings within 2 days.
